title: A copper concentration cell
statement: Two copper electrodes dip in solutions of $\ce{Cu^2+}$ of different strength, joined by a salt bridge and a wire: $c_1 = 0.010\ \text{mol/L}$ at the first electrode and $c_2 = 1.0\ \text{mol/L}$ at the second, at $T = 298.15\ \text{K}$. Find the reaction quotient $Q$, the cell potential $E$ and the free energy change $\Delta G$, and say which way the cell runs.

artefact.caption: The copper concentration cell at $c_1 = 0.010\ \text{mol/L}$: its reaction quotient, potential and free energy change

steps.title: The cell reaction
steps.note: Both electrodes are copper, so the cell has one reaction, the more dilute side dissolving: $\ce{Cu -> Cu^2+ + 2e-}$ at the first electrode and $\ce{Cu^2+ + 2e- -> Cu}$ at the second. It moves $n = 2$ electrons, and the reaction quotient is products over reactants, $Q = \frac{c_1}{c_2} = \frac{0.010}{1.0} = 0.010$.

steps.title: The Nernst equation
steps.note: $E = E^\circ - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q$, and $E^\circ = 0$ for a cell whose two electrodes are the same couple, so $E = -\frac{RT}{nF}\ln 0.010 = 0.0592\ \text{V}$.

answer: $E = 0.0592\ \text{V}$ and $\Delta G = -11.42\ \text{kJ/mol}$: $\Delta G < 0$, so the cell runs as written, the dilute side's electrode dissolving
